findings.statement: The round-7 fix (5c474d0) correctly discharges its stated obligation without the feared unconditional-check regression: I built a standalone harness that calls describe_admission_receipt()/orphaned_mints() directly (not test_hooks.py's fixtures) across 12 adversarial scenarios named in the assignment -- a healthy agent mid-flight holding its only receipt (PASS), a reopened chain where the new agent's receipt clears the old row (PASS) and the superseded agent gets a non-fatal 'none found' rather than a false FAIL, a legitimately consumed-then-disk-deleted receipt (PASS, because the ledger 'consumed' row -- not file presence -- clears it), two agents in one run where the healthy one is unaffected by its sibling's real orphan (PASS) while the orphaned one is correctly blocked (FAIL), and the exact primary target case (one successful mint for agent G masks an earlier failed mint for the SAME agent G) is now correctly caught as a hard FAIL where round-6 bytes silently reported PASS. The per-assignment exclusion (`assignment_id != admitted_assignment_id`) is what makes this possible: it is present, and it is exactly what distinguishes 'this agent's own open receipt' from 'an orphan naming this agent for a different assignment'.
assumptions_used: Direct function-level calls to describe_admission_receipt()/orphaned_mints() in a synthetic .agent-harness tree faithfully exercise the same logic the live SubagentStart hook runs, since inject_subagent_context() calls describe_admission_receipt() with no other gating in between.

findings.statement: The run-scope `--agent-id-unknown` (token-only) orphan check does have a real, reachable, over-broad blast radius -- confirmed empirically: an unrelated, otherwise-healthy agent ('agent-innocent') starting into a run that contains ANY unconsumed token-only mint with no receipt file on disk (for a completely different assignment it has nothing to do with) gets a hard 'Hook preflight: FAIL' at Start. This matches exactly what the module's own docstring says will happen ('a hard FAIL for whichever agent starts next') and is pinned by test_subagentstart_hard_fails_on_an_unattributable_token_only_mint, which explicitly asserts the FAIL recurs under a second, different agent_id ('agent-helper'). A genuinely healthy token-only run with no failed mints anywhere (S4) does NOT trigger this -- the over-breadth requires a prior failed mint to exist in the ledger, which is disclosed as the only way it can fire (admit_agent.py exits non-zero and prints no token when the receipt write fails, so the parent already knows before any agent is spawned against that broken mint). This is a real, disclosed, fixtured, deliberate design trade-off (narrowing it requires --expect-agent-id, which is the required default), not a hidden defect -- so I am recording it as PASS against 'does the documented design hold', while stating plainly that its operational blast radius (every subsequent Start in that run fails until the parent notices and re-mints) is real and should not be read as cost-free.
assumptions_used: 'Reachable in normal operation' is read as: reachable given the documented precondition (one failed --agent-id-unknown mint exists in the run), not reachable with zero failed mints anywhere.
evidence_refs: S8 transcript: agent_id='agent-innocent', ledger has only an unrelated unconsumed token-only mint for X-1 with no receipt file -> verdict FAIL, error text names X-1 explicitly and states the hook cannot tell whether agent-innocent is the agent it was for
S4 transcript (contrast): a token-only run with the SAME mint succeeded and its receipt is present -> verdict PASS
.agent-harness/tests/test_hooks.py test_subagentstart_hard_fails_on_an_unattributable_token_only_mint (asserts the FAIL recurs under a second agent_id)
reproduction: build a synthetic run ledger with one 'minted' row, expected_agent_id='', assignment X-1, and no receipt file for X-1 on disk
call describe_admission_receipt(harness, run_id, 'agent-innocent') -> FAIL naming X-1
repeat with a receipt file present for X-1 (any state) -> PASS, isolating the over-breadth to exactly the 'mint failed, no receipt at all' shape

findings.statement: Round 7 introduces a new, previously-nonexistent blast-radius expansion that is NOT covered by any fixture: a malformed admission-ledger LINE anywhere in the run's ADMISSIONS.jsonl now hard-fails Start's admission check for an agent that holds a perfectly valid, matching, already-open receipt -- a case that PASSED cleanly before round 7. I proved this with an A/B test on an IDENTICAL synthetic fixture (agent-1 holds a valid open receipt for A-1; the ledger has one healthy 'minted' row for A-1 plus one unrelated garbage line) run against both cef6f00 and HEAD 4305533: cef6f00 returns 'open, bound to assignment A-1' (PASS), HEAD returns 'AMBIGUOUS (... ledger line 2 is malformed)' (FAIL). The mechanism: describe_admission_receipt() now reads and validates the ledger unconditionally, and its `if ledger_errors: return AMBIGUOUS` check runs BEFORE classify_receipt_matches() is ever called -- so a matching, open, correctly-bound receipt never gets a chance to short-circuit the malformed-ledger path the way it did in round 6, where the ledger was consulted only inside `if not matches:`. The only existing fixture for a malformed ledger line, test_subagentstart_fails_on_a_malformed_admission_ledger_line, uses an agent with NO receipt at all, so this exact interaction (already-admitted healthy agent + unrelated ledger corruption) has zero fixture coverage. This is NOT a security bypass -- it fails closed, denying an otherwise-legitimate agent rather than wrongly admitting an illegitimate one -- and it is philosophically consistent with the pre-existing (round-6) rule that any unparseable receipt FILE anywhere in the run's admission directory already poisoned every agent's Start check (scan_errors is unconditional and directory-wide, not new). But the ledger-line case specifically is new in round 7, is a real, plausible operational risk (a process killed mid-append to ADMISSIONS.jsonl, or any other single-line corruption), and its consequence is a working agent's HARNESS_RESULT being rejected downstream at Stop (validate_result_contract requires spawn_contract.subagent_start_preflight=='PASS' exactly, and the injected contract instructs the agent to self-report what Start actually said). Per instructions, this fail-verdict finding forces overall status=fail even though my substantive answer to 'was there a regression or bypass' in the security sense is no -- this is a disclosed distinction, not a softened one.
assumptions_used: A malformed line reaching ADMISSIONS.jsonl in production would most plausibly come from a crash/kill mid-append (a partial final line) or direct tampering, both physically possible even though admit_agent.py and subagent_stop_validate.py always write well-formed single-line JSON on the success path.

findings.statement: Cross-run isolation holds: an orphaned mint recorded in one run's ADMISSIONS.jsonl cannot affect Start's admission check for an agent in a different active run. describe_admission_receipt() builds its ledger path as harness/'runs'/active_run/'ADMISSIONS.jsonl', where active_run is read once from .agent-harness/ACTIVE_RUN by the caller -- there is no code path that reads any other run's ledger. Verified directly: a receipt-write failure recorded (and then file-deleted, to simulate the orphan) in run 'runA' has zero effect on a healthy agent admitted in run 'R', which returns 'open, bound to assignment A-1 in run R' exactly as it would with runA absent entirely.
evidence_refs: .codex/hooks/subagent_start_context.py describe_admission_receipt() (ledger_path built from the active_run parameter only)

findings.statement: Every previously-closed Stop-side bypass I re-attacked still holds, on files byte-identical to cef6f00 (subagent_stop_validate.py, admit_agent.py, validate_harness.py, _harness.py all show zero diff across cef6f00..HEAD). I built an independent live-fire harness (not a re-run of test_hooks.py -- different fixture code, a fresh git repo per scenario, direct subprocess invocation of the real hook) and ran 5 fresh attacks: (A) a leaked admission token used by a different agent_id against an --expect-agent-id-pinned receipt -> BLOCKED ('was minted for agent victim-1, not attacker-1'); (A2) the same leaked token against a token-only (--agent-id-unknown) receipt -> ACCEPTED, which is the explicitly documented, unchanged residual mitigated by requiring --expect-agent-id by default, not a new gap; (B) a decoy ACTIVE_RUN pointer combined with NO Start-time lease at all for the stopping agent -> BLOCKED ('No Start-time run lease exists... Refusing to fall back to the mutable ACTIVE_RUN pointer'); (C) a planted .claim file naming the CORRECT eventual holder before any real consume (receipt still 'open') -> BLOCKED ('claim exists ... but the receipt is open with no attribution record'); (D) a symlinked result_path -> BLOCKED ('Declared result artifact is a symlink'). All 5 matched their expected verdict. Additionally: the full test suite is 106/106 (hooks) and 161/161 (all harness tests) on HEAD; the static, read-only `validate_harness.py` reports `ok:true` on the current tree (open_admissions: [], pending_result_count: 0, legacy_results_manifest ok with 136 pinned, ssot_consistency ok); and the committed C6 canary artifact (.agent-harness/runs/run-20260729-f10-d070-canary-c6/artifacts/ACTIVE_RUN_BRACKET_AROUND_CONSUME.json, read as raw evidence, not as a sibling result file) independently confirms a live cross-run decoy-pointer test with both hook SHA-256s pinned to the current frozen bytes (start af8f7016..., stop 0533da88..., matching what I independently recomputed from the real repo) and a 0.036s bracket around the true consume instant, entirely inside the consumed_at second, with the pointer at the decoy run throughout. Chain-age ceiling, declared-reopen supersession/undeclared-second-consume rejection, and the legacy-manifest three-surface pin were re-confirmed via the unchanged-bytes argument plus the green 161-test suite and the clean static validator run rather than via a fresh independent re-derivation of each; that is a narrower confirmation than the 5 live-fire attacks above and is stated as such.
assumptions_used: Byte-for-byte file identity across cef6f00..HEAD (confirmed by `git diff --stat`) plus an unchanged, still-green, previously mutation-tested fixture suite is treated as sufficient evidence of 'no regression' for mechanisms I did not additionally re-derive from scratch (chain-age ceiling, legacy-manifest three-surface pin, forward attribution sweep, merge attribution gate, --reopen laundering).
